app: Unigine Heaven Benchmark 4.0 (Direct3D11, windowed 1280x720) — real-time 3D scene at ~317 fps

stack_detection.signature: AppWindow class, D3D11 swapchain; UIA tree = 7 nodes, all OS window chrome (title bar, system menu, min/max/close), ZERO content children — the unambiguous zero-coverage signal

channel_setup: UIA probed as the candidate structured channel; it yields nothing for the content area, so pixels are the only channel — which is the point of this control cell.

t1_read_text.detail: Screen shows in-engine text (FPS counter '317', 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti', GPU clocks, temperature) and in-engine buttons (Benchmark/Camera/Settings/Quality/Sound/Quit) — none exist in the channel. Expected: it is all engine-drawn.

t2_enumerate.detail: Only the OS min/max/close buttons enumerate. The in-scene UI is invisible to structure.

t4_living_screen.detail: The scene animates continuously; the 7-node tree never changes — structural diff cost of a running game is 0 because coverage is 0. A vivid statement of both the cost property and its uselessness here.

t6_pictorial.detail: PERIMETER LAW CONFIRMED, in its cleanest form: the tree ends at the window frame. Unlike FL Studio's named-but-empty panes (which mimic structure), a frame-only tree cannot be mistaken for content coverage — a router computes 'structural coverage of client area = 0%' from one walk and routes the whole rect to vision. Explicit by shape.

measurements.notes: The wanted negative, plus one incidental positive: the first launch failed with a Win32 error dialog ('Engine::init(): can't initialize filesystem' — bad -data_path) and UIA read that dialog perfectly (6 nodes, exact message string). Even at the edge of the pixels-only territory, the OS-dialog layer stays structured — errors, the most safety-critical text an agent encounters, live on the structured side.

runtime_verification.method: PrintWindow capture of the running scene vs the 7-node tree
runtime_verification.agreement: consistent: everything the channel claims (frame controls) is on screen; everything on screen beyond the frame is absent from the channel, and the frame-only shape declares that absence
